transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
Hi doctor. I’m here because I've been struggling with eating really huge amounts of food. When these episodes happen, I feel a complete lack of control and like I just can't stop myself.
After these episodes, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?
No, I don't do any of those things. I've never tried to make myself throw up, use laxatives, or fast to make up for the eating.
Outside of the eating episodes, have you been feeling down or depressed most days for at least two weeks?

I'm not really sure, as I haven't really noticed feeling down outside of those specific times. It's usually only right after I have one of those eating episodes that I feel really depressed and guilty.
During these eating episodes, do you also eat much more quickly than normal, eat until you feel uncomfortably full, eat when you’re not physically hungry, or eat alone because you feel embarrassed?

Yes, during those times I definitely eat much faster than I normally would. I also find myself consuming huge amounts of food even when I'm not feeling physically hungry at all. It's really distressing how quickly it all happens.
How often have these binge-eating episodes been happening, and for about how many months has this been going on?
This has been going on for about four months now. On average, these eating episodes have been happening at least once a week.

This continues to strongly support Binge-Eating Disorder, and no new information suggests a different diagnosis from the allowed list.
